title: もっと広い家に引っ越そう  (Let Us Move to a Bigger House)

segments.t: From zero contracts to number one in the entire company, Muranishi comes home beaming with his sales award. Over dinner he promises toys to the children and a bigger home to his wife Sachiko. Listen to the family celebrate.
今月の営業成績は一位だったぞ！
本当に？信じられない！
今度リカちゃんハウスを買ってやる。
絶対約束だからね！
大輔にはカウンタックのラジコンを買ってやる。
大丈夫なの？そんな約束をして。
ああ、大丈夫だ。
もっと広い家に引っ越そうな。
楽しみね。
はいはい、任せとけ。
でも仕事のほうはうまくいってよかったじゃない。
期待してますよ。
Happy family talk is full of warm promises and future plans. Let's look at the building blocks.
今月の営業成績は一位だったぞ！
'My sales record this month was number one!' "Kongetsu" means this month, "seiseki" is your score or performance record, and "ichii" puts "ichi", one, with rank-counter "i" for first place.
信じられない！
'I cannot believe it!' Built from "shinjiru", to believe, "shinjirarenai" means 'unbelievable!'—used equally for great surprises and shocking news.
今度リカちゃんハウスを買ってやる。
'Next time I will buy you a Licca-chan dollhouse.' "Kondo" means next time or soon. Attaching "katte yaru" to "kau", to buy, shows a dad proudly treating his kid.
絶対約束だからね！
'That is an absolute promise, okay!' Pairing "zettai", no matter what, with "yakusoku", promise, pins him down so he cannot back out.
大丈夫なの？
'Is it really okay?' You already know "daijoubu" as 'all right'; adding rising "nano" asks 'are you sure that is really okay?'
もっと広い家に引っ越そうな。

'Let us move to a bigger house, too.' When talking about rooms and houses, Japanese uses "hiroi", spacious or wide, rather than 'big'. Turning "hikkosu", to move house, into "hikkosou na" warmly says 'let us move!'
楽しみね。
'Something to look forward to, is it not?' Whenever an upcoming trip, meal, or plan excites you, "tanoshimi" says 'I cannot wait!'
はいはい、任せとけ。
'Yes, yes, leave it to me.' "Makasetoke" squeezes "makasete oke", leave it in my hands, into confident dad-talk.
でも仕事のほうはうまくいってよかったじゃない。

'Still, I am so glad things went well with your work.' "Umaku iku" literally means 'go deliciously or skillfully'—the everyday phrase for things working out smoothly, capped with "yokatta", thank goodness!
期待してますよ。
'I am counting on you.' Built on "kitai", expectation or hope, Sachiko's playful polite "kitai shite masu yo" cheers her own husband on. Now let's listen to the whole family celebration again.
今月の営業成績は一位だったぞ！
本当に？信じられない！
今度リカちゃんハウスを買ってやる。
絶対約束だからね！
大輔にはカウンタックのラジコンを買ってやる。
大丈夫なの？そんな約束をして。
ああ、大丈夫だ。
もっと広い家に引っ越そうな。
楽しみね。
はいはい、任せとけ。
でも仕事のほうはうまくいってよかったじゃない。
期待してますよ。
Keep "shinjirarenai" for 'unbelievable!', "tanoshimi" when you look forward to something, and "umaku iku" whenever plans work out well. In the next scene, morning brings a sudden shock at the office.
おやすみ、また明日。
